key_insight: ESI-Bench reframes spatial intelligence by treating the observer as an active actor: agents must act to acquire observations and reason about how those observations change, enabling inference of occluded structure, dynamics, containment and function that passive sensing cannot resolve.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap where prior work assumes oracle or static observations—preventing evaluation and development of agents that close the perception–action loop and actively discover unseen spatial properties.
method: Recast the perception problem as an embodied control task: design tasks that require agents to choose actions to reduce uncertainty about 3D structure, dynamics and functional relationships.
Provide ESI-Bench — a simulation benchmark and toolkit with diverse environments, task definitions, and evaluation metrics that quantify how well agents close the perception–action loop.
Include baseline agent protocols and standardized metrics (e.g., information gain, task success per action cost) to enable reproducible comparison and progress tracking.
impact: Enables development and standardized evaluation of agents that actively sense and reason about the world, accelerating progress in embodied AI, robotics, interactive perception, and downstream applications that require understanding of occluded and functional scene properties.
visual_elements: Perception–Action loop diagram: agent selects action → new observation → updated belief, repeated; highlight closed loop.
Before vs After comparison: passive (single-shot) view failing to resolve occlusion vs active exploration revealing hidden structure.
Task montage: small panels showing representative tasks (occlusion discovery, containment testing, dynamic interaction) with agent trajectories overlaid.
Metric visualization: 2D chart plotting uncertainty reduction or task success rate against number of actions (efficiency curve) or leaderboard-style comparison.
paper_title: ESI-Bench: Towards Embodied Spatial Intelligence that Closes the Perception-Action Loop
paper_authors: Yining Hong, Jiageng Liu, Han Yin, Manling Li, Leonidas Guibas
